title: Five measured-mass planets exceed the 2021 TRICERATOPS count for 16 high-FPP TOIs under independent hosts
abstract: We test published 2021 TRICERATOPS probabilities with bounds that allow any outcome for unresolved candidates. Sixteen TOIs with reported false-positive probability at least 0.93 contain five planets with measured masses. Their largest expected planet count is 0.49 after a 0.005 rounding allowance. Under independent hosts, the exact upper-tail probability is 0.00005475. A correction for all 78 published-probability cutoffs, two endpoints and three period diagnostics gives 0.00887. This test does not model selection for follow-up or count other statistical validations as planets. All 16 targets have distinct TIC identifiers. The result does not hold without dependence assumptions: the sharp upper probability with arbitrary dependence is 0.098. One of the five discoveries predates 2021; the adjusted probability using only four later discoveries is 0.148. An allowance of 0.02 in each reported probability also removes the rejection. Thus the extreme published probabilities fail a count test under independent hosts, but a strict later-outcome test is not decisive. We provide code, aggregate results, mathematical checks and exact frozen-input retrieval instructions. We do not infer a general correction factor or test the current TRICERATOPS version.

display.caption: Measured-mass endpoint: known-planet count ranges and the largest model mean after a rounding allowance. Tail tests depend on the assumed relation between host outcomes. Bounds are unadjusted; the text gives cutoff-search corrections.
